nodes.title: macOS menu roles missing Tahoe icons and Preferences not renamed to Settings
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.7.0, 41.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.4

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.6.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. Any menu titled "Preferences" should be automatically renamed to "Settings" and the Tahoe settings icon applied.
2. Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit, Minimize, and Zoom (created using their appropriate roles) have their appropriate Tahoe icons applied.

### Actual Behavior

Since the feature for dynamically updating menu properties such as title (PR: #49973), this happens instead:

1. Any "Preferences" menu is left as is and no Tahoe settings icon applied.
2. All the other menus listed above no longer have their Tahoe icons.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/24d89b4614106d6f0000ea2e1a86c871

### Additional Information

In the Testcase, look at the following menus between 40.6.1 and 40.7 (also 41.x, which has the problem):

1. Preferences
2. Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit, Minimize, Zoom

nodes.title: [Feature Request]: Per-WebContents Color Scheme Override
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description Electron currently allows color scheme configuration only globally through [`nativeTheme.themeSource`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/native-theme). For apps with multiple views or mixed UI contexts, this is limiting, because one view may need light mode while another needs dark mode at the same time. This behavior can be demonstrated in Chromium DevTools using CSS media emulation for prefers-color-scheme (see attached screenshot). ### Proposed Solution Expose a per-view API for WebContents, for example: `webContents.setColorScheme()`. Possible values could be like [`themeSource`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/native-theme#nativethemethemesource). This would allow overriding prefers-color-scheme per WebContents without affecting the entire app theme source. ### Alternatives Considered Using Chromium DevTools emulation directly (for example, `Emulate CSS media feature prefers-color-scheme`) is useful for debugging, but it is not a production API and is not suitable as a runtime solution in Electron apps. ### Additional Information _No response_

For apps with multiple views or mixed UI contexts, this is limiting, because one view may need light mode while another needs dark mode at the same time. This behavior can be demonstrated in Chromium DevTools using CSS media emulation for prefers-color-scheme (see attached screenshot). ### Proposed Solution Vystavení metody pro nastavení color scheme, například: `webContents.setColorScheme()` Expose a per-view API for WebContents, for example: `webContents.setColorScheme()` Possible values could be like [`themeSource`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/native-theme#nativethemethemesource) This would allow overriding prefers-color-scheme per WebContents without affecting the entire app theme source. ### Alternatives Considered Using Chromium DevTools emulation directly (for example, `Emulate CSS media feature prefers-color-scheme`) is useful for debugging, but it is not a production API and is not suitable as a runtime solution in Electron apps. Why this matters Per-view theming is useful for: - apps embedding multiple independent surfaces - side panels or tools that should keep a fixed theme - gradual migrations between light and dark UI - testing and accessibility scenarios without global side effects ### Additional Information _No response_

nodes.title: Transparency not working when using BaseWindow on Ubuntu (using Xorg)
Support org.freedesktop.portal.Secret backend for safeStorage on Linux
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The [safeStorage API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/safe-storage) currently has those backends on Linux:
- `basic_text`
- `gnome_libsecret`
- `kwallet`
- `kwallet5`
- `kwallet6`

The `basic_text` provider stores items unprotected using a hardcoded password. I think you can see why this is not optimal.

The others use the appropiate system key chain depending on which is available. This is generally fine. However, if an app is packed as [flatpak](https://flatpak.org/), this requires giving it talk permissions for the appropiate dbus path. This is discouraged because of security concerns. The intended way is to use the [`org.freedesktop.portal.Secret`](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.Secret.html) portal, which electron currently does not implement.

### Proposed Solution

Add a new safeStorage backend that uses the portal. The portal gives an application an unique string, that it can use to encrypt its secrets. This synergizes well with the `basic_text` backend, which already does this. Just instead of a hardcoded password, use the one provided by the Secrets Portal.

### Alternatives Considered

Require every flatpak app to continue using extended permissions, resulting in Warnings both on the webpage and during installation.

### Additional Information

I am not sure how to handle a transition. If this is implemented, and a flatpak removes the talk permissions, old secrets will be unavailable. Same case if both backends can be used, but we default to the portal. If we do not default to the portal, it will never be adapted

nodes.title: Frameless window sometimes drags while resizing for MAS-built applications
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.8.4, 41.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.3

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.0.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When resizing a frameless window within an Electron application packaged for MAS, the window should only be resized, and not be moved / dragged.

### Actual Behavior

The window will sometimes move / drag while simultaneously being resized. This doesn't occur consistently, but happens more frequently when resizing from the corners, particularly when the mouse is as close to the middle of the window as it can be, while still allowing the resize to occur.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Since this requires the application to be packaged for MAS, I couldn't provide a gist, but I have a repo available under [https://github.com/mgalla10/frameless-window-resize](https://github.com/mgalla10/frameless-window-resize), built off of the electron/minimal-repro repo.

This is reproducible via a packaged build alone; signing is not required. If you wish to sign, you'll need to provide your own cert / provisioning profile.

This looks to be largely related to [issue 49770](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49770), which was fixed in v40.6.0. However, the fix doesn't appear to be fully sufficient. From looking at the actual changes made to patches/chromium/mas_avoid_private_macos_api_usage.patch.patch, I'm guessing the 5.0 resize threshold isn't large enough in all cases - at the very least, it might explain why the issue is easier to reproduce when the mouse is at a window corner, and at the edge of the resizable range.

When resizing a frameless window within an Electron application packaged for MAS, the window should only be resized, and not be moved / dragged.

The window will sometimes move / drag while simultaneously being resized. This doesn't occur consistently, but happens more frequently when resizing from the corners, particularly when the mouse is as close to the middle of the window as it can be, while still allowing the resize to occur.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Since this requires the application to be packaged for MAS, I couldn't provide a gist, but I have a repo available under [https://github.com/mgalla10/frameless-window-resize](https://github.com/mgalla10/frameless-window-resize), built off of the electron/minimal-repro repo.

This is reproducible via a packaged build alone; signing is not required. If you wish to sign, you'll need to provide your own cert / provisioning profile.

This looks to be largely related to [issue 49770](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49770), which was fixed in v40.6.0. However, the fix doesn't appear to be fully sufficient. From looking at the actual changes made to patches/chromium/mas_avoid_private_macos_api_usage.patch.patch, I'm guessing the 5.0 resize threshold isn't large enough in all cases - at the very least, it might explain why the issue is easier to reproduce when the mouse is at a window corner, and at the edge of the resizable range.

### Expected Behavior

- Packaged app should behave exactly like the unpacked electron . version regarding GPU acceleration.
- NVIDIA “Background Application Max Frame Rate” should only affect background windows, not the active foreground app.
- --disable-gpu (and --disable-gpu-compositing) should force software (CPU) rendering, causing CPU usage to rise and GPU usage to drop to near zero.

### Actual Behavior

When running an Electron app directly with `electron .` (unpacked), GPU acceleration works perfectly: CSS animations are buttery smooth and GPU usage is normal.

After packaging the same app into `app.exe` (using any bundler/packager — tested with electron-builder, electron-forge, etc.), the following two issues appear:

1. **NVIDIA Control Panel throttling bug**  
   Even when the app is the **active foreground window**, NVIDIA’s “Background Application Max Frame Rate” setting (e.g. 30 FPS) still limits the frame rate, causing severe stuttering/lag in CSS animations.  
   The same setting has no effect on the unpacked `electron .` version.

2. **`--disable-gpu` does NOT fall back to CPU/software rendering**  
   Adding `--disable-gpu` (or `--disable-gpu-compositing`) makes animations smooth again, **but CPU usage stays low** while GPU usage spikes to extremely high levels (often 80-100% on a dedicated NVIDIA card).  
   This proves `--disable-gpu` is not correctly disabling hardware acceleration; instead the app is still using the GPU in a broken/inefficient way.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information
- Adding --disable-gpu, --disable-gpu-compositing, --disable-software-rasterizer, --use-gl=swiftshader, or --enable-features=UseSoftwareCompositing does not resolve the high GPU usage.
- The only “fix” that restores smoothness is --disable-gpu, but it incurs extremely high GPU load.
- This issue only appears after packaging; the development version is unaffected.

nodes.title: GPU process on Wayland lacks --ozone-platform and DrmSyncobj flags (5x CPU overhead)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.0.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43, GNOME/Mutter, Wayland, Intel integrated GPU

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The GPU process should receive the same Wayland/GPU acceleration flags as standalone Chromium 146, enabling zero-copy buffer sharing and hardware-accelerated compositing via DRM render nodes.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process spawns as a zygote child (`--type=zygote --no-sandbox`) without any Wayland or GPU acceleration flags. This produces the error on every launch:

```
'--ozone-platform=wayland' is not compatible with Vulkan.
Consider switching to '--ozone-platform=x11' or disabling Vulkan
```

The GPU compositor falls back to a software/GL path, compositing on the CPU before submitting to the GPU.

**GPU process flags comparison:**

Chromium 146 GPU process (working efficiently):
```
--type=gpu-process
--ozone-platform=wayland
--render-node-override=/dev/dri/renderD128
--enable-features=WaylandLinuxDrmSyncobj,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL
```

Electron 41 GPU process (software fallback):
```
--type=zygote --no-sandbox
(no ozone, no render-node, no features)
```

The acceleration features ARE present in Electron's network/utility child processes but are NOT propagated to the zygote-spawned GPU child.

### Testcase Gist URL

_This issue cannot be reproduced in Electron Fiddle — it is a process-level GPU spawning issue visible only via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and GPU profiling. See profiling data below._

### Additional Information

#### Profiling data (8h overnight, identical content)

We built a digital signage player that runs on both Electron and standalone Chromium. Same PWA, same layouts, same machine. Here is the comparison:

**CPU usage by process type:**

| Process | Electron 41 | Chromium 146 | Ratio |
|---------|-------------|--------------|-------|
| GPU | 22% | 1.3% | **17x** |
| Renderer | 17.5% | 1.9% | **9x** |
| Main | 8.5% | 1.2% | **7x** |
| **Total** | **48.5%** | **5.5%** | **9x** |

**GPU memory (PSS, proportional):**

| | Electron 41 | Chromium 146 |
|---|---|---|
| GPU process PSS | 524 → 950 MB (growing) | 83 → 85 MB (stable) |
| DRM render engine time | 2,590s | 320s |

#### GPU memory leak

The GPU PSS grows from 524 MB to 950+ MB over 8 hours (texture accumulation from the software compositing path). Standalone Chromium's GPU stays flat at ~85 MB.

#### Related issues

This appears related to #36633 (Zero GPU Acceleration on Wayland, open since Electron 22). That issue has 38 comments and was last active in 2023.

#### Environment details

- Both Electron 40 (Chrome 144) and Electron 41 (Chrome 146) exhibit the same behavior
- Standalone Chromium 146.0.7680.80 on the same machine has zero GPU issues
- The fix landed in Chromium between 144-146 via `WaylandLinuxDrmSyncobj`, but Electron's zygote-based GPU spawning does not inherit these flags
- Intel integrated GPU with DRM render node at `/dev/dri/renderD128`

#### Possible workaround

Would passing `--in-process-gpu` merge the GPU compositor into the main process (which does have the correct features)? We have not tested this yet.

### Electron Version

40.5.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 15

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.4.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

This is a documentation issue. I'm not sure how to submit issues for this other than as a bug report. I apologise if this is the wrong way to do it.

Documentation: https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/native-code-and-electron-swift-macos#6-creating-a-javascript-wrapper

Since Electron 40.5.0, there has been a change in how it closes down, due to a change in Node, and as a result, there's an issue with native modules following the examples in the documentation.

The current example for the Native module actually causes Electron to hang when trying to quit. This is because the callbacks are held without being destroyed on quit, not allowing the destructor to run. This keeps the native node module active, and with the changes to Node never lets Electron quit, even though the quit event fires.

The documentation needs to include a destroy function or similar, which is then called when the app is quitting. An example destroy function is as follows:

```
    Napi::Value Destroy(const Napi::CallbackInfo& info) {
        callbacks.Reset();
        emitter.Reset();

        if (tsfn_ != nullptr) {
            napi_release_threadsafe_function(tsfn_, napi_tsfn_abort);
            tsfn_ = nullptr;
        }

        return info.Env().Undefined();
    }
```

This should be called during quit (code below to go in the JS wrapper):

```
async destroy () {
   await this.addin.destroy()
}
```

### Actual Behavior

Missing destroy function in documentation.

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: NodeService SIGSEGV on Wayland Window Destruction (Hybrid Graphics)
nodes.body:
## 📌 Description
Closing a secondary Webview utility window in an Electron/Chromium-based application reliably triggers a fatal `SIGSEGV (Signal 11)` core dump on Native Wayland.

The crash occurs exclusively during the window/buffer destruct sequence, pointing to a regression in Chromium's Ozone Wayland layer handling surface destruction while the `--render-node-override` GPU channel is still established.

## 💻 Environment
* **OS:** Linux (Fedora/Nobara)
* **Kernel:** Hybrid Graphics Stack (AMD/NVIDIA)
* **Display Server:** Native Wayland
* **Chromium Feature:** `EarlyEstablishGpuChannel,EstablishGpuChannelAsync` 

## 💥 Crash Extracted Trace (systemd-coredump)
```text
           PID: 790034
           UID: 1000 
        Signal: 11 (SEGV)
  Command Line: /proc/self/exe --type=utility --utility-sub-type=node.mojom.NodeService --lang=en-US --service-sandbox-type=none --render-node-override=/dev/dri/renderD128 --enable-features=EarlyEstablishGpuChannel,EstablishGpuChannelAsync
       Message: Process 790034 of user 1000 dumped core.
                
                Stack trace of thread 790034:
                #0  0x00007fb9eaab3775 n/a (n/a + 0x0)
                ELF object binary architecture: AMD x86-64
```

## 🔍 Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch an application on a native Wayland Linux distribution using hybrid graphics.
2. Ensure Chromium dynamically defaults to `--ozone-platform=wayland`.
3. Open a secondary Webview utility which spawns an isolated `node.mojom.NodeService` worker.
4. Close the specific Webview panel.
5. `systemd-coredump` intercepts an immediate `SIGSEGV` core dump from the child NodeService trying to interact with `/dev/dri/renderD128` post-surface-destruction.

## ⚠️ Notes
- Passing `--disable-gpu` or `--disable-software-rasterizer` via `.desktop` files or `argv.json` **DOES NOT PREVENT THIS BUG**. The parent process physically strips those overrides when forking the Webview and manually forces `EarlyEstablishGpuChannel` into the child process execution string.
- Using `export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` mitigates the buffer bindings at the Mesa API layer but does not fix the underlying Chromium Ozone destruction timing flaw.
- Forcing `--ozone-platform=x11` (XWayland mode) currently completely stops the crash from occurring because XWayland buffers the destruction natively.

### Expected Behavior

Calling `window.print` from the render process or `webContents.print` from the main process will print the current page contents.

### Actual Behavior

No print dialog appears. The callback passed to `webContents.print` isn't run until the app closes.

```javascript
webContents.print(); // failureReason: Invalid printer settings
```
